$comment: The cast: the nine major parts of Overview §2 and three terms of Overview §7 (trust anchor, state proof, running hash). plain is the everyday description; spec paraphrases the overview's definition, with the Protocol module that defines the term cited after it.

cast.name: Ledger
cast.plain: A network that keeps its own records and runs smart contracts, such as a Hiero network or an EVM ledger. A channel connects two of them.
cast.spec: A distributed ledger with smart contracts and state proofs. It runs at least one CLPR Service, and exactly one on Hiero. Each ledger has its own Ledger Specifications.

cast.name: Application
cast.plain: The program that wants to talk to another ledger. It sends messages through the CLPR Service, receives the messages sent to it, and later receives the reply to each message it sent.
cast.spec: A contract that sends and receives messages through the CLPR Service. Each ledger defines the callback interface through which messages and replies are delivered to it.

cast.name: CLPR Service
cast.plain: The protocol's own part of each ledger. It keeps the outbound queues, hands each bundle to the channel's verifier, checks message order itself, delivers messages to applications, and, under the recommended design, holds each connector's stake and collects its charges.
cast.spec: The component that implements CLPR on a ledger and holds its CLPR state: a native service on Hiero, a smart contract on EVM ledgers.

cast.name: Channel
cast.plain: A standing connection between two ledgers, with an outbound queue on each side and a fixed verifier for checking the other side's proofs.
cast.spec: A connection between the CLPR Services of two ledgers, with the same id on both. Each side has an outbound queue and a verifier contract. Several channels can connect the same ledgers.

cast.name: Verifier contract
cast.plain: The specialist that knows how to check one particular ledger's proofs. Each channel picks one when it is opened and keeps it for life, though the contract may be upgradeable.
cast.spec: A stateless contract, fixed when a channel is opened, that checks the peer ledger's proofs against the trust anchor stored with the channel. Before using a channel, an application should evaluate its verifier, including whether it is upgradeable and who controls the upgrades.

cast.name: Trust anchor
cast.plain: What the verifier checks the other ledger's proofs against, such as that ledger's identity or its current validators. Stored with the channel, and changed only by a bundle that the current trust anchor accepts.
cast.spec: The data, stored with the channel, against which the verifier checks proofs; its content is defined by the proof scheme. It is set when the channel is opened and changed only by bundle processing, from the verifier's output.

cast.name: Connector
cast.plain: The account that pays. It authorizes a message on the sending side and pays for running it on the receiving side. If it breaks that promise, its stake is slashed.
cast.spec: An economic actor on both ledgers of a channel. It authorizes messages on the source ledger and pays for their execution on the destination. Its stake can be slashed.

cast.name: Endpoint
cast.plain: The program that carries bundles between ledgers. It exchanges bundles with endpoints on the other side and submits what it receives as an ordinary transaction. It cannot forge a message; with a correct verifier it can only delay one.
cast.spec: A CLPR Endpoint: a node that exchanges bundles with endpoints of the peer ledger and submits received bundles to its own ledger. On Hiero every consensus node is one; on EVM ledgers endpoints register and are admitted by the administrator. Endpoints are not slashed.

cast.name: Message
cast.plain: A parcel of bytes plus an address. Three kinds share one queue: data (what applications send), replies (the answer to a data message), and control (protocol housekeeping).
cast.spec: One unit of communication on a channel: application data (DATA), a reply (REPLY) or a control message (CONTROL). Every DATA message receives exactly one REPLY, in the order of the original messages.

cast.name: Bundle
cast.plain: Usually a batch of messages, with one proof of the sender's channel state and of the last message.
cast.spec: The proven state of one side of a channel, usually with a contiguous run of messages from its outbound queue. The proof covers the last message; the running hash binds the ones before it.

cast.name: State proof
cast.plain: A sealed receipt from a whole network, showing that a specific piece of data really is in its records.
cast.spec: A proof that data is part of a ledger's committed state. Each ledger verifies the other ledger's state proofs directly, with no intermediary network.

cast.name: Running hash
cast.plain: A hash of everything one side has sent on a channel, updated with each message so that the receiving CLPR Service, with a correct verifier, notices anything inserted, removed or reordered.
cast.spec: A hash chain over a queue's messages, which the receiver recomputes and compares with the proven running hash of the bundle's last message. Both sides start the chain from the same fixed value.
